Geschichte.et: From Middle High German geschicht(e) (“event, struggle, story, history”), from Old High German gisciht, from the verb Proto-Germanic *skehaną, whence German geschehen. Unrelated to Schicht. Cognate with Bavarian Gschicht and Vilamovian gyśicht.

geschickt.et: From Middle High German geschicket (“arranged, prepared, ready, suitable”), synchronically analyzable as the past participle of schicken.

Geschirr.et: From Middle High German geschirre (“harness, gear”), from Old High German giskirri, giscirri (literally “the trimmed (thing)”), from skeran (“to shear”), from Proto-Germanic *skeraną. Cognate with Alemannic German Geschirr.

Geschick.et: From Middle High German geschicke (“occurrence, incident; disposition”), with semantic narrowing to "conditions and fate". See the related schicken (“to send”) for more.
